problem:
Let X be a connected compact complex manifold of dimension n>=3, h a smooth positive Hermitian form, and dV a smooth positive probability volume. Suppose the bounded-potential lower Monge-Ampere mass v_-(h) is zero. Use dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial. Let G_h be the positive (n-1,n-1)-currents T with dd^c T=0 and integral h wedge T=1. In an h-unitary frame, write sigma_T=h wedge T and the positive Hermitian matrix density P_T characterized by beta wedge T=(1/n)tr(B P_T)d sigma_T, tr P_T=n, where B is the matrix of a smooth (1,1)-form beta relative to h. For a real continuous logarithmic density F, set Gamma_F(T)=(exp(F)dV/h^n)^(1/n) det(P_T)^(1/n) sigma_T and D_F(T)=Gamma_F(T)(X). The attained maximum M(F)>0 equals exp(-B_0(F)/n), where B_0(F) is the scalar in MA_h(u)=exp(B_0(F)+F)dV. For every exact maximizing current T, the determinant-weighted probability nu_(T,F)=Gamma_F(T)/M(F) is absolutely continuous with respect to dV and represents an adjoint/supporting probability of B_0. If F is smooth, the exact maximizing current is unique, smooth and strictly positive: it is the normalized (n-1)st power of the Gauduchon form conformal to the smooth solution form. In the smooth case Gamma_F(T)=exp(F/n)k_T dV with k_T=(gamma^n/dV)^((n-1)/n) for T=gamma^(n-1), respecting trace normalization. At an actual maximizer one can equivalently define its determinant density by k_T=exp(-F/n)M(F)d nu_(T,F)/dV.

Original S17 asks whether a uniform critical L^(n/(n-1)) estimate can hold for the determinant-weighted probabilities of exact maximizing currents representing adjoints, uniformly as F ranges over a specified bounded set, when v_-(h)=0. Identify geometric or density hypotheses giving such a restricted estimate. Specify the bounded family, its topology/quantitative bounds, whether all its data are smooth or continuous, and whether the estimated density is k_T or d nu_(T,F)/dV. The endpoint can fail for the full normalized Gauduchon test family, whereas every strictly smaller exponent has a universal estimate. Positive lower mass gives the full endpoint, but is excluded here. One fixed smooth strictly positive density has a unique smooth maximizer; this fact is background and is not a uniform theorem over a family. Near-maximizing sequences can have divergent higher moments even on Kahler manifolds. Distinguish exact maximizers from all tests and from near-maximizers. No candidate density family, geometric condition, estimate or proof is supplied.
